## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

This record covers [Issue #238](https://github.com/kjelly/pilot/issues/238) and the
[capability acceptance contract](../../superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-cache-capability-readiness-spec.md).
The machine section is the final fresh two-node topology chain; the native Go
cache and consumer arms below used the same immutable candidate and binary.

The dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 KVM cache host used Docker 29.1.3, Compose 2.40.3,
Harbor 2.15.1, Pulp 3.85.25 and kernel 6.8.0-124. Twelve official cached images
were copied read-only; repository digests and ordered layer/runtime-config
fingerprints matched after loading. Two independent candidate archive checkouts,
executable copies and separate VM data directories used one shared service root.
Identities, credentials and network addresses were synthetic; artifacts were public upstream packages/images or purpose-built test data.

| Native arm | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Partial initialization | Initial up failed after 125.928 s. With global running still false, an APT-only VM provisioned in 25.305 s, completed cloud-init and its selected configuration checks, then tore down successfully. |
| Explicit fixture completion | A subsequent repair failed on the Pulp task before its synthetic HTTPS origin was trusted. Adding the test CA to that existing native remote preserved TLS verification; completion repair passed in 104.220 s. The normal startup/repair errors are retained as failures, not successful commands. |
| Healthy shared startup | Two independent startup processes retained all 11 container IDs/start times and configuration, credential, CA and state bytes/mtimes. |
| Readonly probes and cancellation | Repeated status retained those invariants. A 3 s loopback delay plus real SIGTERM returned context-canceled failure 0.003 s after the signal; state/configuration and service lifecycle remained unchanged. |
| Legacy client policy | Removing only persisted descriptors and denying Harbor administration still allowed APT and OCI VMs. OCI used the independent executable/checkout. No descriptors were backfilled; physical fingerprint, CA, generation and container lifecycle stayed unchanged. |
| Descriptor-only changes | A profile without an OCI descriptor refused OCI before domain creation. Adding its readonly immutable descriptor allowed consumption without repair, recreation or changing the physical fingerprint. |
| Harbor management HTTP 401 | Native health and independently verified public data remained usable; explicit APT, RPM and OCI VMs completed cloud-init and their selected file checks. Management startup refused the wrong credential without mutation. |
| APT unavailable | Required APT refused before domain creation; an OCI-only VM succeeded. The mixed topology union refused before creating any node. |
| Management ready, OCI data denied | Making the synthetic project private retained healthy native Harbor status and authenticated management, but refused the OCI consumer. An APT-only VM succeeded. Restoring public access restored the data probe. |
| Pulp unavailable | Required RPM refused before domain creation; APT-only consumption succeeded. Explicit container restoration recovered native health and data. |
| Valid-auth maintenance protection | With a live OCI consumer, repair, down and confirmed purge all refused specifically at the consumer gate, with unchanged service lifecycle. |
| Mixed topology | The final fresh two-node chain passed syntax, check/diff, apply, 4/4 verification rows with zero failures/skips, and second apply changed=0 on both nodes. Actual inventory groups and APT-only versus OCI-only files were asserted on each node; both domains were removed. |

The APT proof used Ubuntu hello 2.10-3build1 with SHA-256
`e68cf4365b7aa9c4e2af4af6eee1710d6f967059b7b4af62786e8870d7366333`;
a guest also completed real apt metadata/package retrieval. Pulp served native
RPM metadata and the 6,216-byte data-only fixture package, SHA-256
`44e06ac8a98cbd5121d6d0623e2916cfb860cd210e21b5f0b3dbbb10f19e7f6e`.
Go and guest OCI reads used the immutable BusyBox manifest digest
`sha256:a7dbc319b1438115a207e11930dc4bb3e643dcb3ec0bdd694bb36cd8fad289ec`,
including the native anonymous Bearer challenge. A native Docker pull completed.

The first topology attempt reached successful per-node check/apply assertions but
the external spec lacked the required numbered checklist heading. The next
attempt correctly refused its undeclared target scope. After linting the corrected
fixture and supplying the explicit observed inventory selector all, the entire
fresh chain was rerun and the success record above was generated. Neither row
expectation nor production source was weakened. A postflight wrapper initially
expected the machine marker before the generated title; strict inspection of
the actual JSON schema, candidate, binary, outcome and final state corrected that
wrapper assertion without changing the successful chain record.

Local checks on the tested commit passed: 368 package tests/subtests, the same
368 under race detection, 26 selected CLI cases and 518 importer cases; no test
was skipped. The command package with no test files emitted a package-level
no-test event. Build-all, vet, formatting and golangci-lint 2.12.1 passed.
Fourteen independent semantic mutations failed their intended assertions,
including selection, native bodies, cancellation/publication and policy identity.
The real strace/SIGTERM pre-rename preservation and retry tests executed.

The automatic redaction section covers the Ansible chain inputs. A separate scan
of 126 native output/JSON/record files checked five runtime credential/private-CA
sources, raw/basic-auth/JSON-escaped forms and the wrong-admin sentinel: zero
matches. Source fixture definitions were excluded from that output scan.
All nested guest domains were absent after testing; the owned outer cache VM
and its overlay were removed after private evidence capture. Existing operational
services and unrelated VMs were outside the mutation boundary.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

Supported sharing is one OS user across processes, checkouts and VM state
directories. Cross-user sharing, production capacity, full RPM installation,
upstream bandwidth savings, concurrent miss coalescing and offline/cache-hit
accounting are not established. The native OCI evidence proves actual authorized
digest-checked cache reads; it does not claim that every Docker mirror/fallback
configuration or a clean-client layer bandwidth benchmark was tested.

The first startup still required explicit retry; deterministic first-attempt
Harbor readiness is not claimed. Readonly means no implicit render, prepare,
Compose lifecycle changes, seed or credential repair; normal GETs may populate native caches.
The partial/legacy and fault arms cover the declared synthetic resources, not
every possible artifact or service failure. A volatile InRelease development
probe exceeded its 2 s request bound after injected network delay and correctly
refused readiness; the final matrix used the immutable package descriptor above.

The controller was native, not the optional pinned controller profile. The
